The tip plate of the bow may be made of bone, ivory, mammoth ivory, or metal. A bow maker or archetier typically uses between 150 and 200 hairs from the tail of a horse for a violin bow. The violin typically has four strings, usually tuned in perfect fifths with notes G3, D4, A4, E5, and is most commonly played by drawing a bow across its strings. The A string is first tuned to a standard pitch (usually A=440 Hz). The violin is the smallest and thus highest-pitched instrument in the family in regular use.
